purpose: Execute the main ADLX event interpreter, its wait exits and its OPL voice operations over the shared C/SOUND audio owner. Produce ordered register-write events; retain timer scheduling, section restoration, effects allocation and hardware in their existing boundaries.

original.classification: Behavioral L1-to-L2 migration of assembly-origin code. No exact ASM/C byte claim or alteration to L0. L0-to-L1 link remains differential.
original.voice_services: Native main semantics include SetAdlibChannelVolume/KeyOffAdlibChannel/SetAdlibFrequency/SetAdlibChannelGain/LoadAdlibInstrument and ordered WriteAdlibRegister behavior; global L1 driver endpoints remain for effects/C callers.

native.bridge: All ten main interpreter entries replaced together. Native step owns persistent values and ordered OPL events. Bridge retains scratch registers/flags, wrapping fetch, timer capability call and platform output. Explicit L1 fallback for modified dispatch table or instrument source overlapping the live/displaced voice arrays; audits distinguish these.

inputs: AudioState: all raw words/bytes admitted, including noncanonical flags, reserved counts and slot words
Already-fetched opcode and twelve stable operand bytes; AudioCursor points past the opcode
Operation enum permits the direct wait/handler entries as well as decoded opcode entry
outputs: Updated typed shared audio state and cursor; CONTINUE, WAIT or END
Ordered list of at most fourteen OPL register/value writes, not a final register map
Optional BE16 timer-period request; bridge delivers the real TIMER interval call
effects: Frequency/key-off/gain/instrument affect the selected live or displaced voice, with deliberately distinct routing gates
Wait advances the main deadline and publishes only cursor index, leaving its resource half untouched
END decrements signed repeats or retains infinite-repeat state; expires descriptor active bit or resets cursor/deadline/time-origin; never clears playing
No sample mixer, DMA, allocation, scanning, section application or scheduler replacement
preconditions: Serialized ordinary RAM; no mid-event IRQ or observation of individual RAM stores
Immutable disjoint event operands. Instrument source overlapping voice destinations uses explicit bridge fallback
Canonical event dispatch table for native interpreter control; modified tables use L1 fallback
Borrowed bridge event windows refer to accessible machine RAM, not memory-mapped VGA; canonical dedicated disjoint stack
Finite interpreter burst or explicit bridge budget of 1000000 events; malformed endless no-wait streams are outside termination claims

callers.normal: SOUND:TickAdlxPlayback loads ES:DI from descriptor12, preserves ES/DI/BX around the far interpreter call and later restores AX/BX/DX. CX/SI/DS and IF/DF can flow; bridge preserves the complete existing L1 register shell as well.
callers.section_boundary: Before calling main interpreter, Tick compares cursor OFFSET ONLY against MainAdlxSectionEnd when loop-enable bit0 is set, calls C:ApplyScannedMusicEvents, and reloads the cursor. That C service restores scanned voices and advances origin. No section comparison occurs inside an event burst.
callers.direct: Nine reconstructed handler entries remain callable for existing direct differential tests; their opcode has already been fetched.

callees.native: Internal volume/level/write helpers only. Original OPL service behavior is implemented inside the native step, not called through L1.
callees.boundary: TIMER:SetTimerCallbackInterval, platform_out. L1 DelaySoundIo state contract is reconstructed in bridge; CPU busy-loop elapsed time has no deterministic service points.
callees.other_interpreter: Effects interpreter remains L1: RunEffectAdlxEvents plus seven looping handlers and long/short waits; END expires through C:StopAdlibTrackChannel -> RestoreAdlibVoiceAllocation, including voice compaction and ordered restoration. It requires record8..11, current record selector, first_voice, step_q8 and shared live/displaced voices.

indirect.main_dispatch: Fixed complete 16-entry target set: long wait, frequency, key off, gain, instrument, no-op, timer period, control, then eight copies of short wait. Native enum removes the machine jump table; bridge validates all entries.
indirect.external: Only TIMER interval setter; no callback invocation inside a native event. Effects C stop/allocation boundary is not closed.

memory.owner: Common C/SOUND audio storage. native/audio.h is one typed borrowed view, not independent copies for original C and driver.
memory.channels: 13 records, original base0014 stride002A. All scalar cells retained; sample-only meanings remain opaque to this closure. start/cursor become borrowed-window cursors. Record12 occupies020C..0235. Main start0212, length0216, cursor021C, deadline022A, voice_count022E, control0234 are aliases of channels[12]. No duplicated absolute main fields in AudioState.
memory.voices: Three nine-entry views live0278, displaced032C, scanned03E0, stride20. Twelve instrument working bytes, volume+0C, gain+0E, owner+10, frequency+12. SOUND symbol consumers establish these names; architecture-model prose reverses gain/volume. Opcode3 writes gain+0E; two-stage high-byte scaling applies gain before volume+0C. High stale bytes preserved on byte writes.
memory.clocks: Guard0236, rate0238, ticks023A dword, origin023E dword, scanned_ticks0242 dword; upper-word aliases are interior views. playing0256 and section_loop_enabled025C are distinct raw words outside record12. No conflation of descriptor active, playing, repeat and section enable.
memory.fade_and_sections: Fade step/duration/start/target0246..024C, scheduled0258 and handle1124; section start025E and end0262 far cursors. Projection retains all; interpreter does not advance fade or apply sections. PIT period000C and playback handle1122 retained separately from ticks and rate.
memory.writes: Main deadline/cursor/repeat/control/origin and selected voice values; timer period on6n. Bridge republishes equal retained voice bytes in ordinary RAM. No raw-memory-store-journal equivalence is claimed. Ordered OPL writes are compared exactly.

assumptions: No canonical boolean, reserved-count<=9, on-screen or shipped-state restriction on a one-event state
One-event symbolic cut terminates at the next fetch; induction requires valid stable operands and the same external TIMER contract on each step
TIMER request observer proves request equivalence, not scheduler internals; compiled differential/scenario/host checks use the real maintained timer
Delay busy loops have no state/device effects beyond the retained CF/OF product flags; exact CPU-cycle timing is not an observation
Shipped-stream exhaustion is finite corpus coverage C; it is not exhaustive over every possible byte stream
eliminated: Machine register/segment/stack spelling from ordinary native C; bridge preserves existing ABI
Recursive table-tail control replaced with native enum step and iterative bridge fetch
Original hardware register access replaced with ordered semantic events delivered by platform layer
retained: 16-bit long-wait delta truncation before 32-bit deadline addition
Main displaced key-off clears LOW word bit5, live key-off clears B0 key bit
Distinct frequency/key, gain, instrument and volume reservation gates; byte-width 9-reserved threshold
Invalid1n/4n channel>=9 consumes no operand; invalid3n still consumes one;5n consumes none
Instrument copies12 bytes but advances11;12th byte is the next opcode and is retained
Instrument write order includes01=20 between carrier80 andE0, before feedback and final level refresh
77 signed old repeat<=1 expires, including8000; repeat copies clock and cursor without advancing current fetch cursor
70 consumes length plus two bytes irrespective of length; other7n except77 skips length bytes
No section check inside event loop; caller offset-only boundary and original scanner quirks remain
